techniques.title: Reuse the same key when a tool retries
techniques.outcome: Prevents double-charges on payment or deploy retries.
techniques.teaser: When a tool call is retried after a dropped ack, reuse the same idempotency key — a fresh key double-charges.
techniques.whatWhy: Agents that retry payments, posts, or deploys after a timeout often mint a new key each try. That creates duplicate side effects. A gate that requires a stable key per logical order blocks release when retries would double-charge.
techniques.howTested: Offline structural sim (no live model): 5 drop_ack charge episodes. Stable keys: 0 I1 violations (one charge each). Fresh UUID keys: 5 of 5 double-charges; gate blocked release on that pattern.

techniques.title: Require held-out lift before shipping harness edits
techniques.outcome: Stops train-only tweaks that fail on new cases.
techniques.teaser: Don't ship a prompt or middleware tweak on in-dev lift alone — require positive held-out lift first.
techniques.whatWhy: Harness edits that look great on the training set can collapse on held-out cases. Selecting by train lift alone ships the brittle option. A gate that requires held-out mean lift and non-negative worst-case held-out delta picks the version that transfers.
techniques.howTested: Offline structural sim (no live model): two mock harnesses A (train overfit) vs B (transfers). Train-only selection shipped A (held lift −0.15). Held-out + worst-Δ gate shipped B (held lift +0.143).

techniques.title: Load only the tools this turn needs
techniques.outcome: Cuts prompt size without losing the needed tool.
techniques.teaser: Don't dump every tool schema into context — search and load only the ones this turn needs.
techniques.whatWhy: Large tool catalogs burn tokens when every schema is always loaded. Deferred load via keyword search keeps the needed tool available while cutting prompt size. A bad query negative control confirms the search can miss when it should.
techniques.howTested: Offline structural sim (no live model): 8-tool catalog. Naive load-all used 1530 mock tokens; tool-search top path used 220 (−85.6%) with needed tool still available; bad query correctly left needed tool unavailable.

bodyMarkdown:
# AI Digest — Tue Sep 16, 2026

Mode: offline structural box tests (no live model on box).

## News FYI

- Gemini 3.8 Live / Live Extended Thinking (Google, Sep 15): live dialogue with background tool use while conversing.
- GPT-6 Astra + Codex harness speed (OpenAI, vendor numbers — not re-run here): Astra rolling to limited orgs; Codex harness claimed ~1.9× faster computer-use task completion vs prior on Mind2Web.
- Harness research: HarnessDev (arXiv:2609.01437) — self-evolved harnesses unstable / partial held-out transfer; Beyond Prompts / PRISM (arXiv:2609.05736) — held-out lift reporting for harness edits.

## Techniques

### Reuse the same key when a tool retries

Agents that retry payments, posts, or deploys after a timeout often mint a new key each try. That creates duplicate side effects. A gate that requires a stable key per logical order blocks release when retries would double-charge.

Stable keys: 0 I1 violations across 5 drop_ack episodes. Fresh UUID keys: 5 of 5 double-charges; the gate blocked release.

### Require held-out lift before shipping harness edits

Harness edits that look great on the training set can collapse on held-out cases. Selecting by train lift alone ships the brittle option. Require held-out mean lift and non-negative worst-case held-out delta before adopting.

Train-only selection shipped brittle A (held lift −0.15). Held-out gate shipped B (held lift +0.143).

### Load only the tools this turn needs

Large tool catalogs burn tokens when every schema is always loaded. Search and load only what this turn needs.

Naive load-all: 1530 mock tokens. Tool-search path: 220 tokens (−85.6%) with the needed tool still available; bad query negative control caught.
